messages:
laura: Heads-up: starting ~16:05 UTC we saw a p95 jump from ~120ms -> 420ms and p99 spikes to ~1.2s for hosted text-gen in us-east-1. Noticing queue depth climb to ~180 on the inference nodes.

mike-rte: Seen it, correlates with a sudden increase in small-seq requests from one tenant. Request rate stable overall but our batching sampler produced many small batches.

sara-ml: Profiling snapshot (sampling profiler) attached: hot functions show fallback matmul kernels and high memcpy activity. Looks like kernel selector favored fallback path after some kernel-autotune miss.

laura: Paste of kernel selection logs from one affected worker: 
```
[2024-04-25T16:05:12Z] model=redwood-v2 size=1 seq=64 kernel=fast_gemm chosen_score=0.92
[2024-04-25T16:05:12Z] model=redwood-v2 size=1 seq=128 kernel=fallback_matmul chosen_score=0.31 reason=cache_miss
[2024-04-25T16:05:13Z] batching_sampler: batch_size=4 target_latency_ms=120 sampled_seq_mean=110 sampled_seq_std=60
[2024-04-25T16:05:13Z] kvcache: evict_count=243 evict_rate=0.14
```

nate-sre: kvcache evictions look high. If kernel fallback triggers >1.5x memory, that can cause eviction thrash and extra memcpy -> extra latency. Any noisy neighbor tenant id?

mike-rte: Tenant t-712 spiked small short prompts; sampler changed distribution and started creating more heterogeneous batches which pushed kernel selector threshold below fast_gemm.

ops-oncall: Deploy-bot triggered canary fallback rollback? deploy-bot: automatic-rollback: triggered for commit abc123 (kernel-heuristics). Canary flag toggled off at 16:08:21 UTC.

laura: After rollback p95 dropped to ~140ms then stabilized ~130ms over 3 minutes. p99 still has occasional blips.

sara-ml: I ran a targeted microbenchmark on the 2 kernels:
```
# benchmark results (single step, seq=128)
fast_gemm: 8.4ms
fallback_matmul: 20.1ms
memcpy_overhead: +6ms (when evicitons > 100)
```

mike-rte: Root cause hypothesis: the recent change in batching_sampler introduced an aggressive seq variance estimator which classed many mixed-length microbatches as high variance -> lower confidence in precompiled kernel -> fall back to generic matmul. That plus sudden small-seq bursts from t-712 increased memory churn (kvcache evictions) which amplified memcpy overhead.

nate-sre: Action items: 1) throttle t-712 spikes (temp tenant quota) 2) revert sampler tuning permanently until we add warmup probe 3) add metric to kernel-selector to expose chosen_score distribution 4) adjust kvcache eviction threshold to be less aggressive under transient variance.

laura: I've applied a temporary quota on t-712 (rate limit lowered by 60%) and increased kvcache soft-cap by 15% on hot workers. Monitoring now.

ops-oncall: Current graphs: queue depth trending down from 180 -> 30 in 2min, p95 back to baseline, p99 occasional 700-900ms for single hosts only.

sara-ml: I'll push a patch to batching_sampler: add a 30s sliding warmup probe that forces a few deterministic batches for kernel scoring before switching heuristics. Draft PR coming (link: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/742).

mike-rte: For immediate observability, add these logs: `kernel_selector.chosen_score` and `batching_sampler.sampled_seq_std`. Also add a perf counter for `kvcache.evictions_per_min`.

laura: Leaving a note for post-incident: run a focused experiment to measure kernel decision boundary: vary sampled_seq_std from 10 -> 120 and record chosen kernel + latency. We should get an S-curve.

nate-sre: Will open a short postmortem once metrics settle. For now, mark incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

laura: Thanks everyone. Lessons: kernel heuristics + noisy small-seq traffic can produce emergent memory pressure via kvcache churn. Need better pre-probing and per-tenant burst controls.

mike-rte: /cc product infra and customer success (possible noisy tenant outreach).

deploy-bot: canary-rollback: complete (timestamp=2024-04-25T16:09:02Z).
